liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (3 reviews): The Shakedown jam is strong, with Jerry playing horn-like notes and Brent funky on synths, though not especially tight; Jerry and Brent get really funky in Shakedown, which flows into a standout Bertha [13][16][23]
- **Tennessee Jed** (2 reviews): Jerry's playing is singled out as wailing on Tennessee Jed, along with Big River, Loser and Althea; Tennessee Jed is described as a phenomenal, big version worth hearing [17][22]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): The He's Gone into The Other One segment is called killer; He's Gone into The Other One is singled out as smokin' [14][23]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer, whose favorite song is Jack Straw, says this opening version is one they replay repeatedly [24]
- **Big River** (1 review): Big River is described as incendiary [22]
- **Althea** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Althea as very strong [14]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Reviewer says this is the best Lost Sailor they have heard [17]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls this their pick for the best Stella Blue [14]

## The recordings

- **gd79-11-25.sbd.miller.25609.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 4.5/5 by 28 [1]. Said about its sound: Slight hiss on this copy, but called the best available version at the time; Charlie Miller version said to be a perfect copy with no hiss, better than other 1979 recordings; Sound quality is great, but track numbering seems off: Tennessee Jed appears as d1t2 and d1t3, and d1t1 is tuning [16][19][20][22]
- **gd79-11-25.sbd.dan.7192.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 169 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has short digital noise spikes in several tracks, easily removed with a wave editor; the sound is otherwise terrific; This copy has noise reduction applied, most noticeable between songs; an upgrade was expected [13][15]
- **gd1979-11-25.sbd.miller.84489.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 4.33/5 by 18 [4]. Said about its sound: Easy To Love You dropouts were smoothed with crossfades, and numerous static pops were removed with Cool Edit Pro [4]
- **gd1979-11-25.179232.sbd.miller.flac1648**: soundboard; 22 songs; 171 min [5]
- **gd1979-11-25.aud.severson.minches.90720.flac1644**: audience recording; 22 songs; 176 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer thinks the second set has the most going on [16]
- Reviewer calls this their favorite first set, and says the Charlie Miller version of 2004 is much better [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-11-25.sbd.miller.25609.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: A cut in Bertha appears to have been patched; Soundboard to master cassette to PCM to DAT, transferred via Sony R500 DAT, SEK'D Prodif Plus and Samplitude, then SHN; Patch source was a Nakamichi 700 master cassette to reel to CD, possibly one more reel generation, via Charlie Miller [1][23]
- **gd79-11-25.sbd.dan.7192.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1979-11-25.sbd.miller.84489.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) [4]. Also: Patch source discs were provided by David Hollister; patches cover Drums, Space and Bertha, using soundboard master reel MP3 [4]
- **gd1979-11-25.179232.sbd.miller.flac1648**: transferred by Mastered by Charlie Miller  September 13, 2026; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Maxell UDXL-II/Dolby B) [5]. Also: Combines three sources: a soundboard patch upsampled to match, and an audience patch recorded by Mark Severson [5]
- **gd1979-11-25.aud.severson.minches.90720.flac1644**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by David Minches; source: 2 Sony ECM-270s on stand 40' from stage> Sony TC-D5 (2 Maxell UD XL-IIs) [7]. Also: A brief patch near 6:24 uses Bob Menke's recording, made with two Nakamichi CM-700 mics into Sony TC-D5 [7]
